results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

The reader names usage-metering-and-rating as its own chapter in Part VI, payment links as a brief mention (a hosted payment page, no mechanism), and ERP posting as left out by decision with RECONCILED as the place to go. All three parts of expected are present.

The reader says the model is the author's unpublished Productscape model of 29 bricks in four groups, reviewed 15 November 2026; that it describes no company's internal systems and may not be cited for Stripe; and names clearing, card vaults and 3-D Secure as added chapters. Matches expected.

From the introduction alone the reader predicts the capability-to-chapter tables group by group with grades, then the brief and left-out list with where to go instead, the ten subjects, the added subjects and the role routes, from the model and the book's chapters, with the model stated not to be evidence. This contains the substance of expected. The reader's doubts (where the ten subjects come from; Part VIII) are noted under flow and known_before_new.
All 17 prose units and the two introduction callouts summarize to the controlling idea of the spec unit they align to, in the spec's order.
Introduction ¶1: two phrases flagged by the outliner are the two halves of p01's single controlling idea (the model lacks the mechanisms, so this page sends a job to its chapter).
One Map, Three Answers ¶1: the synthesis and the practical rules are the conclusion's declared synthesis and takeaway, delivered together as the spec's conclusion asks; one idea in two halves.

Every body unit serves S1-S5 (model ¶1-3 to S1; coverage ¶1-2 to S2; brief ¶1-2 to S3; ten subjects to S4; added ¶1-2 to S5; readers ¶1-2 to S2/S5). The intro ¶2 and conclusion ¶2 are declared transition units that help a reader find the neighbouring reference pages. Nothing a lookup reader would have to skip past.

Each table is introduced by a sentence saying what it shows (shape of the model; tally and mechanism-versus-surface pattern; nine below chapter level and why; parts left out and where to go; every subject has chapters; what the model has beside what the book adds; five of six scenarios have a nearest chapter; role routes), and the model quotation is followed by what the book does with it. The one inaccurate summary sentence (brief ¶1) is recorded under flow_is_followable.

All declared boundaries except p15 express their relationship at the start of the unit ('To place that lookup', 'The page itself runs', 'Because the model is', 'With those rules in place', 'complete the map in the same way', 'Twenty ... nine do not', 'Beyond whole capabilities', 'The model was not the book's starting point', 'Because the book started from those ten subjects', 'as an example', 'also reuses', 'Taken together'), and the closing unit links the toolkit as the hand-off.

results.draft_locus: The Model's Customers and the Book's Readers ¶2
results.quote: By contrast with the routes, the question differs.
results.finding: The declared contrast is between the five roles' outcomes and the engineer's question. The opening sentence contrasts 'the routes' with an unnamed 'question', so it neither picks up the roles' outcomes nor says what differs; both flow readers had to re-read it. Something like 'The roles ask about outcomes; the engineer who builds for them asks something else' would carry the declared relationship.

Both flow readers describe the order as model first, then the full map, then the gaps each way, then reading routes, matching the declared large_to_small pattern and the roadmap; neither marks any section's position unclear. The material lost-thread points are recorded as separate failures.

results.draft_locus: The Ten Subjects the Book Set Out to Cover ¶1
results.quote: The model was not the book's starting point.
results.finding: Both readers had read the opening ('The planning model behind this book') as meaning the book was planned from the model, so this fact arrived as a surprise in the fourth section and made them re-read the coverage tables. The section can stay where the spec puts it; the prose before it (the opening or 'Where the Model Comes From') should say once that the model served as a check on the author's list of ten subjects.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item 3 (fourth bullet); flow reader A, item 3 (fourth bullet)

results.quote: So Parts I, IV and VIII have few or no bricks behind them.
results.finding: The page never says what Parts I, IV and VIII are; Part IV in particular is never identified, so a reader cannot tell which chapters the claim is about. Name what each part covers in a few words, or drop the part numbers.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item 3 (first bullet); flow reader A, item 3 (second bullet)

results.draft_locus: The Ten Subjects the Book Set Out to Cover ¶1
results.quote: the ten map onto the book's parts almost one to one

results.draft_locus: What the Book Covers Briefly or Leaves Out ¶1
results.quote: Those nine are either product surfaces or separately licensed products
results.finding: The table that follows contradicts the summary: delegated authority is below chapter level because it was unreleased at the cut-off, and reporting because it is taught as an input to reconciliation; neither is a product surface or a separately licensed product. Both readers had to reconcile the sentence with the rows. Qualify it (most are product surfaces or separate products; one is mostly unreleased). The spec's p09 controlling idea carries the same overstatement and should be loosened to match when the author next edits the spec.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, item 3 (sixth bullet); flow reader A, item 3 (sixth bullet)

results.quote: The second row deserves a closer look
results.finding: The reader had to go back and count rows in the previous table to find which row is meant. Name it ('The six stress scenarios deserve a closer look').

results.quote: With those rules in place, a row of the tables reads as follows.
results.finding: A reader who jumps to the tables and wants the grade definitions has to hunt for them under the heading 'Where the Model Comes From', which does not announce them. The heading is fixed by the spec, so the remedy (a sub-heading or a pointer from 'Coverage by Capability' back to the grade definitions) is the author's call.
Brick, key, grade, Productscape model, Larkfield, RECONCILED and ORDERED are defined at or before first use; the terms that are not are recorded as failures below.

results.quote: all of Part VIII have no capability in the model
results.finding: Part VIII is used in the KEY POINTS before the page says what it is; it is only explained in a table row in 'What the Book Added'. A few words ('Part VIII, on running the system at scale') would fix it.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader A, item 3 (tenth bullet); flow reader B, item 3 (first bullet)

results.quote: Four dated milestones in a tutorial
results.finding: The model's contents are listed in 'Where the Model Comes From' (bricks, offerings, roles, records, scenarios, comparison list) without a tutorial, so this row uses a part of the model the reader has not met. Mention the tutorial (and its single walkthrough, used two rows later) when the model's contents are listed, or gloss it in the row.

The introduction opens with a direct statement of the model and the five mechanisms it lacks, says what the page is for, places it among the reference pages and gives a roadmap; none of the weak patterns.

The conclusion synthesizes three kinds of lookup answer and their common cause, calls back to the opening and gives a course of action and a hand-off; it adds no new subject and does not merely restate the thesis.

'one of three answers to a lookup' and their single cause (model by what can be bought, book by what happens to the money) is stated by no single section, and the closing sentence says what a reader should do with it.

'That also answers the opening. The 29 capabilities name no clearing, vault, 3-D Secure, idempotency or versioning because those are mechanisms beneath the products' returns to the hook named in callback.to.
